# [PR #19444] [None][fix] Synchronize disaggregated KV receive destinations

source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19444
state: closed | updated: 2026-09-23T03:47:42Z
labels: ci: full pre-merge approved

## 正文

V2 KV cache admission can queue a partial-reuse copy that races with an
incoming disaggregated KV transfer, overwriting received data. Wait for
the cache stream before publishing receive destinations.

Add regression coverage for synchronous and asynchronous receives,
empty admission, fence failures, and a simulated GPU overwrite race.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Dev Engineer Review

- `KVCacheManagerV2` now records a per-request CUDA event after cache preparation and waits for it before publishing disaggregated KV receive destinations.
- Event state is cleaned up when requests are released or the manager shuts down.
- The public `synchronize_for_disagg_receive` method was removed. Callers must use the updated admission flow.
- `scheduler_v2.py` changes documentation only. No runtime behavior changes.
- Review-finding counts are unavailable from the supplied results.

## QA Engineer Review

- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_disagg_receive_ordering.py` adds coverage for synchronous and asynchronous receives, selected-request synchronization, repeated and failed admission, cancellation cleanup, event refresh, and the GPU overwrite race.
- The test file covers both success and error paths for disaggregated KV admission.
- No `tests/integration/test_lists/` files changed, and no matching test-list entry was found.
- Coverage verdict: **needs follow-up**. The adapted regression suite passed, but running the current test file unchanged remained outstanding.

## Per-File QA Perspective

- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager_v2.py`: Verify per-request event recording, selective waits, failure handling, destination publication, and cleanup. Verify callers no longer use the removed method.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/scheduler/scheduler_v2.py`: Verify that the updated documentation matches the existing inline allocation behavior. No runtime change is expected.
- `tests/unittest/_torch/executor/test_disagg_receive_ordering.py`: Verify event ordering, failure paths, cleanup, repeated admission, and the simulated overwrite race for both transfer modes. The unit test is not listed in the integration test lists.

### xwang233 · 2026-09-22

Hi @SimengLiu-nv and @chienchunhung, thank you for the reviews. I revised the fix to record and wait on per-request CUDA events instead of synchronizing the full stream. Responses below.

```bash
> The PR identified a real bug.
> My concerns are:
> 1. if the sync is only needed for KVCM V2, it's probably a bug. Working around in on the executor loop seems like an overkill.
> 2. stream sync is expensive, especially on the execution stream. We should find cheaper ways to fix this race.
```

Agreed. The local revision moves the fence into `KVCacheManagerV2`: successful admission records a CUDA event, and `prepare_resources` waits for it before receive destinations are published. The V2-specific executor sync is removed.

This avoids waiting for work queued after the event, but the manager shares the execution stream, so earlier forward work can still block the wait. The benchmarks show similar performance to full-stream sync; they don’t demonstrate a speedup.

> The proposed fence addresses the reported race in V2 kv cache manager. Could we avoid draining the shared execution stream for every nonempty receive batch, or provide benchmarks showing the throughput impact is acceptable?
>
> PS: V1 may have a similar ordering gap, which is worth investigating in a separate follow-up.

The local revision replaces the full-stream sync with a per-request event recorded at admission. Regression coverage checks that work queued after that event remains pending when receive starts.

GSM8K accuracy recovered to the full-stream-sync baseline range. Throughput was comparable to full-stream sync, with a small observed reduction versus the incorrect unfenced baseline.

Validation used a compatible backport onto the original experiment image, with repeated measurements in separate allocations per variant. The adapted regression suite passed; running the current test file unchanged remains outstanding.

Agreed that V1 warrants a separate investigation.
